chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When you have finished the two cycles (of prayer), go to the Black Stone, kiss it, and touch it, or gesture towards it, for it is necessary to do so.

And he (peace be upon him) said: If you are able to drink from the water of Zamzam before you go out to Al-Safa, then do so, and say when you drink: 'O Allah, make it beneficial knowledge, abundant sustenance, and healing from every illness and disease.'

He (peace be upon him) said: And it has reached us that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said when he looked at Zamzam: 'Had it not been that I would burden my community, I would have taken from it a bucket or two buckets.'

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa (one of the hills in Mecca)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended rituals regarding the Black Stone and Zamzam water during Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith establishes the Black Stone as a focal point for spiritual connection following the two-cycle prayer (Salat al-Hajj), emphasizing the physical act of kissing or gesturing as an act of reverence rather than worship. The instruction to drink Zamzam before proceeding to Al-Safa highlights the ritual purity and spiritual preparation required for the Sa'i, while the prophetic tradition underscores the principle of *ease* (*yusr*) in Islamic law, explaining why the Prophet did not make it obligatory to prevent hardship for the Ummah.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya and Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When you are free from (Praying) the two Cycles, so go to the Black Stone and kiss it, and touch it, or gesture towards it, for it is a must from that’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If are able to drink from the water of Zamzam before you go out to Al-Safa, then do so, and you should be saying when you drink:
اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْهُ عِلْماً نَافِعاً وَ رِزْقاً وَاسِعاً وَ شِفَاءً مِنْ كُلِّ دَاءٍ وَ سُقْمٍ
‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Make it to be a beneficial knowledge, and an extended sustenance, and a healing from every illness and disease’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And it has reached us that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said when he<sup>saww</sup> looked at Zamzam: ‘Had it not been difficult upon my<sup>saww</sup> community, I<sup>saww</sup> would have taken from it, a bucket or two buckets (thereby creating a Sunnah)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya and ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that after performing two Rak‘at salat (prayer) you should go to the Black Stone, kiss, touch it and point toward it; it should be done.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘If you can drink from Zamzam before leaving for al-Safa’, it is better, and when drinking say, ‘O Allah, make it useful knowledge, abundant sustenance and a cure for all illnesses and deficiencies.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘It has come to us that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, when looking at Zamzam, said, ‘Were I not to cause difficulties for my followers, I would have taken one or two containers full of water of Zamzam.’”
